slides.headline: History's Shortest War Killed 500 People
slides.body: Britain calls it a 38-minute trivia record. Zanzibar counts roughly 500 dead in the rubble of a burned palace.

slides.headline: A Treaty Zanzibar Never Agreed To
slides.body: An 1886 pact let Britain approve every Zanzibari sultan. In 1896, Khalid bin Barghash took the throne without asking.

slides.headline: The Royal Navy Opens Fire at 9:02
slides.body: Five British warships shelled the sultan's palace for 38 minutes straight, reducing it to splinters and burying whoever was still inside.

slides.headline: About 500 Zanzibaris Died in Minutes
slides.body: The Royal Navy logged one British sailor injured. Historians estimate roughly 500 Zanzibaris killed or wounded in the same 38 minutes.

slides.headline: Empires Turn Massacres Into Trivia
slides.body: Call it the shortest war and the deaths disappear into a punchline. The record survives; the 500 dead do not get named.

slides.headline: Whose War Gets Remembered as a Joke?
slides.body: Britain still holds the world record for its shortest war. Zanzibar has never gotten an apology for its longest one.
